text:
sara: Heads up — saw ~40 tiny GPU jobs (0.25 GPU each) stuck Pending in us-west2. Dashboard shows warmpools sitting idle in other racks but scheduler isn't packing them across rack-iso taints. Cost spike on warmpool hours and user impact. Anyone seen this pattern? :eyes:

matt_dev: Yep saw the same alert. Pod events show nodeSelector + topologySpread + rack taint combo failing scheduling.

anika: Can you paste the `kubectl describe` for one of the pending pods? Curious which constraint is dominant.

sara: paste below

```
Events:
  Type    Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----    ------            ----  ----               -------
  Warning FailedScheduling  2m    default-scheduler  0/24 nodes are available: 16 node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeSelector, 8 node(s) had taint "rack/iso:NoSchedule" that the pod didn't tolerate, 24 node(s) Insufficient memory.
```

matt_dev: Hmm the message is weird — says 24 nodes insufficient memory even though these are tiny GPUs. Probably a stale binpacking metric where we reserve memory per GPU flavor.

ben_infra: We recently rolled a rack isolation policy to avoid cross-rack NVLink blasts; it taints some racks with `rack/iso=isolated:NoSchedule` and we rely on topology weights to prefer co-located allocations. Looks like the scheduler's small-pod bypass isn't enabled in us-west2 yet.

ops-oncall: tagging @matt_dev @ben_infra — alerting team. We're seeing user retries and a few timeouts.

matt_dev: Quick triage idea: allow small GPU pods (<0.5 GPU) to ignore the `rack/iso` taint for a short period so the scheduler can pack them into otherwise isolated racks. We can implement as a patch to the kube-scheduler policy or via a mutating webhook adding a toleration for small jobs.

anika: Least invasive might be a temporary mutating webhook that adds toleration `rack/iso:NoSchedule` for pods with annotation `redwood/small-gpu=true`. Then we can revert.

ben_infra: I can flip a flag on the warmpool manager too — reduce reserved memory per slot so the scheduler reports nodes as having capacity. That addresses the "Insufficient memory" false positives. Which do you want first?

ops-oncall: Prioritize quick user relief: webhook toleration + a metric roll on warmpool reservations. I'll run the webhook rollout during low traffic window.

infra-bot: runbook note: Temporary toleration change requires updating `mutatingwebhookconfiguration` and informing security. See: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/rack-iso-temporary-override

matt_dev: I'll draft the webhook patch and test in staging. If that works, ben can adjust warmpool reservations to stop the repeated cost churn.

anika: Also let's add an alert for "small-pod-pending due to rack-iso" so we catch this earlier. Right now it just surfaces as generic Pending which gets noisy.

ben_infra: Agreed. I'll enqueue a small telemetry job to create a metric: count(pods_pending{reason=FailedScheduling, taint=\"rack/iso\"}) by rack.

sara: Thanks team. For immediate users I created a manual workaround for the top 5 traces. Please post when the webhook is in staging so we can validate. :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: ETA for webhook in staging ~25m, will ping here when done.

matt_dev: staging patch applied, scheduling looks better — 30/40 pods moved to running across racks with the toleration in place. Leaving the mutation on for 1h and monitoring.

ops-oncall: Noting cost impact: warmpool drain/repack reduced wasted hours by ~12% during the fix window. We'll measure longer term after warmpool reservation change.

anika: Follow-up items: 1) permanent policy for small-pod packing 2) refine warmpool reservation logic 3) alert rule for rack-iso pendings. I'll add them to the eng-platform board.

sara: awesome — closing this thread once items are tracked. Thanks everyone! :rocket:
